steps: Fit the training event/time target without predictors.

steps: Use a time-indexed target series.
Fit(y_train); predict(fh=horizon).
assumptions: Consistent time index and meaningful last-value baseline.

subjective_assessment.rationale: Cheap reference that should accompany more complex forecasts.

steps: Construct make_reduction(Ridge(), strategy="recursive", window_length=10).
Fit lag generation and regressor inside each temporal training fold.
Predict(fh=horizon); do not use future observed target values as lags.
assumptions: Enough complete history; this recipe does not claim exogenous or panel support.

subjective_assessment.rationale: Practical bridge to sklearn regressors; recursive forecast errors can accumulate.

steps: Encode ordered target levels explicitly; use a full-rank numeric design with no constant.
Construct OrderedModel(y, X, distr="logit"); fit; predict probabilities through the fitted results.
assumptions: Proportional odds.

subjective_assessment.rationale: Interpretable ordinal baseline; ordering and constant handling are critical.

steps: Prepare a finite numeric design and group labels.
Construct MixedLM(y, X, groups); fit.

assumptions: Linear mean and chosen random-effects distribution.

subjective_assessment.rationale: Useful for repeated entities; many random effects can make fitting expensive.

steps: Construct SARIMAX(y_train, order=(1,0,0)); fit.

assumptions: Selected ARIMA specification and residual assumptions.

subjective_assessment.rationale: Strong classical baseline for serial structure; large seasonal state spaces increase cost.

steps: Install distribution cubist; import Cubist from cubist. The compiled C extension requires a supported wheel or a working native build environment.
Supply named numeric and categorical predictors in a pandas DataFrame and a complete one-dimensional numeric target; preserve column names and categorical representation at prediction.

Fit within each training fold; pass aligned nonnegative finite sample_weight if required. Missing predictors are supported by the documented Cubist interface; verify missing and unseen categorical values in deployment probes.
Call predict for numeric predictions; inspect the model and rule/coefficient summaries for interpretation. Keep cv=None when a reusable fitted predictor is needed.
assumptions: Rule conditions partition the predictor space and local linear equations produce predictions; this is regression, not a classifier.
n_committees controls sequential error-correcting models. neighbors=1..9 optionally corrects predictions using training instances; auto=True chooses corrections and requires neighbors=None.
Neighbor correction retains training data and weakens a purely rule-based explanation. Tune rule count, committees and neighbors within training data.
sample_weight is documented as case importance; prediction does not accept observation weights. Evaluation weights remain separate.
cv produces an evaluation report rather than a reusable model. Internal sample/cv options do not replace externally controlled evaluation splits.
Dense in-memory fitting only in this recipe; no partial_fit. Committees, rules and retained neighbor data increase cost. Extrapolation is constrained by the extrapolation parameter.

steps: Install distribution skope-rules; import SkopeRules from skrules. Validate imports and sklearn compatibility in an isolated pinned environment first.
Fit imputation and numeric categorical encoding within each training fold; provide finite dense predictors. Supply feature_names matching the transformed columns.
Explicitly map the class of interest to 1 and the background to 0, with both classes present in training. Multiclass labels must not be passed directly.
Fit without sample_weight in this recipe; tune precision_min, recall_min, max_depth and rule deduplication on training data.

Use predict for rule-union binary predictions, decision_function for precision-weighted rule votes, or score_top_rules/predict_top_rules for ranked-rule decisions; choose thresholds using validation data.
assumptions: Learns short logical rules from bagged trees and screens them using out-of-bag precision/recall; rule scores are not calibrated probabilities.
max_samples<1 leaves observations for out-of-bag screening. Internal OOB scores do not replace independent evaluation; assess minority recall, precision and PR-AUC for class scoping.

The fit signature accepts sample_weight, but upstream transforms it into regression targets for additional candidate-rule trees; it does not apply conventional observation weighting to all fitting and rule evaluation. sample_weight_fit=false deliberately excludes general importance/rebalance weighting from this recipe.
Labels other than zero can be collapsed into the positive class upstream; this recipe requires explicit binary mapping and does not claim native multiclass classification.
There is no predict_proba or partial_fit. Dense encoding, number/depth of trees and candidate-rule evaluation govern memory and time; n_jobs controls bagging parallelism.
